explanations.explanation: Moses, Israel's leader, says it right out: “Destroy completely all the places where the nations you are dispossessing have served their gods…” (Deuteronomy 12:2). He says completely, friend. That's not a tidy-up, that's a whole-kitchen scrub. I'd say that word was picked on purpose.

Moses says the opposite. He says to “Destroy completely all the places…” where the nations served their gods (Deuteronomy 12:2). Leaving them standing is like leaving a tray of burnt cookies on the rack and hoping they get better on their own. These places do not stay.

A wall is a nice idea, friend, but Moses never says it. He says to “Destroy completely all the places…” (Deuteronomy 12:2). Fencing something off is like putting a sticky note on a smoking oven. Moses wants the places gone, and the text gives no middle option.

Moses says, “Tear down their altars, smash their sacred pillars, burn up their Asherah poles, cut down the idols of their gods…” (Deuteronomy 12:3). Look at all those verbs. Tear, smash, burn, cut. That's a to-do list with zero “maybe” on it.

The text says the opposite. Moses says, “Tear down their altars, smash their sacred pillars…” (Deuteronomy 12:3). The altars come down. Moses even adds more verbs after that one, so nobody can say they missed it.

Moses says the opposite: “You shall not worship the LORD your God in this way.” (Deuteronomy 12:4). He has just talked about the nations' altars and poles, and he wants Israel nowhere near that style. So the LORD gets worship His way, not theirs. It's a short verse, friend, but it doesn't wobble.

Moses says it plainly: “You shall not worship the LORD your God in this way.” (Deuteronomy 12:4). The way of the nations is off the table for Israel. Short verse, big line. I'd stamp it on a cookie, but it's already clear enough.
Moses says to seek “the place the LORD your God will choose…” (Deuteronomy 12:5). The choosing belongs to the LORD, not to Israel. Nobody is voting on this one, friend.

The text doesn't hand the choice to the elders. Moses says Israel must seek “the place the LORD your God will choose…” (Deuteronomy 12:5). A committee would still be passing the cookie tray around while the meeting ran long. The LORD does the choosing.
Moses never says the priests choose. He says Israel must seek “the place the LORD your God will choose…” (Deuteronomy 12:5). That place comes from the LORD Himself. Everyone else gets to go there.
Moses says the place is “to establish as a dwelling for His Name” (Deuteronomy 12:5). A dwelling is a home, friend. I think that's a warm picture for a place people come to worship.

Moses doesn't say anything about an army camp. He says the place is “to establish as a dwelling for His Name” (Deuteronomy 12:5). A dwelling is a home, not barracks. Nobody is marching at this place in this verse.
No school shows up in this verse. Moses says the LORD will establish the place “as a dwelling for His Name” (Deuteronomy 12:5). It's a home for His Name. No classrooms, no homework, friend.

Moses says they will “eat and rejoice in all you do, because the LORD your God has blessed you.” (Deuteronomy 12:7). The reason for the joy is the LORD's blessing. Not a trophy, not a number. Just the LORD.

explanations.answer: Their harvest was the biggest yet
explanations.explanation: Moses doesn't say anything about a record harvest. He gives this reason: “because the LORD your God has blessed you.” (Deuteronomy 12:7). Their joy is tied to the LORD's blessing. Nobody is bragging about crop size here.

The text doesn't compare flocks to the nations at all. Moses says they will rejoice “because the LORD your God has blessed you.” (Deuteronomy 12:7). The blessing is the reason. Nobody is counting heads, friend.

explanations.answer: Everyone does what seems right to him
explanations.explanation: Moses says, “You are not to do as we are doing here today, where everyone does what seems right in his own eyes.” (Deuteronomy 12:8). And notice he says “we.” He's not pointing at the crowd with his mustache folded. I mean his arms. Okay, I'm the one with the mustache. Moses is counting himself in.

explanations.answer: Everyone waits for a word from Moses
explanations.explanation: That's not what Moses says. He describes it this way: “where everyone does what seems right in his own eyes.” (Deuteronomy 12:8). Nobody is standing in line for instructions in that verse. Everyone is doing their own thing.

explanations.answer: Everyone follows the ways of Egypt
explanations.explanation: Egypt doesn't come up in this verse. Moses says, “…where everyone does what seems right in his own eyes.” (Deuteronomy 12:8). It's about each person's own eyes. He says “we,” so he's counting himself in.

explanations.answer: They haven't reached their resting place yet
explanations.explanation: Moses says, “For you have not yet come to the resting place and the inheritance that the LORD your God is giving you.” (Deuteronomy 12:9). Notice the word yet. That word tells you something is still coming. They aren't there, but the LORD is giving it to them.

explanations.answer: They haven't built their first altar yet
explanations.explanation: An altar isn't the reason Moses gives. He says, “For you have not yet come to the resting place and the inheritance that the LORD your God is giving you.” (Deuteronomy 12:9). It's about the resting place they haven't reached. The word yet carries the verse.

explanations.answer: The tribes haven't been counted yet
explanations.explanation: Counting tribes isn't in this verse. Moses says, “For you have not yet come to the resting place and the inheritance that the LORD your God is giving you.” (Deuteronomy 12:9). The reason is the resting place. Nobody needs a clipboard.

Moses says, “…and the Levite within your gates, since he has no portion or inheritance among you.” (Deuteronomy 12:12). A Levite is a man from the tribe set apart for service to the LORD. He's named in the rejoicing list. The more the merrier, friend.
Close, but that verse names someone else. Moses lists “the Levite within your gates” (Deuteronomy 12:12). The word gates matches, but the person doesn't. The Levite is the one on the list.

Elders aren't in that list. After the sons, daughters, menservants and maidservants, Moses names “the Levite within your gates” (Deuteronomy 12:12). The Levite is the person he adds. That's who's on the guest list.

Moses says the Levite is within their gates, “since he has no portion or inheritance among you.” (Deuteronomy 12:12). That's the reason Moses gives. The Levite is named right there with the family. I think it's a kind detail, and I'll stand by that.

The text gives exactly that reason. Moses says, “…and the Levite within your gates, since he has no portion or inheritance among you.” (Deuteronomy 12:12). So the statement is true. The Levite has no portion or inheritance among them, and he's named in the rejoicing.

Moses says the opposite: “Be careful not to offer your burnt offerings in just any place you see;” (Deuteronomy 12:13). Then he says to offer them “only in the place the LORD will choose…” (Deuteronomy 12:14). The word only is doing the heavy lifting. A burnt offering doesn't go wherever a person happens to be standing.

Right, Moses says not to do that. He says, “Be careful not to offer your burnt offerings in just any place you see;” (Deuteronomy 12:13). Then he says, “…you must offer them only in the place the LORD will choose in one of your tribal territories…” (Deuteronomy 12:14). So it's one place, and the LORD chooses it.
Moses says, “…you may slaughter and eat meat within any of your gates…” (Deuteronomy 12:15). That means at home, friend, in their own towns. No trip to the chosen place needed for this one.
No priest's tent in this verse. Moses says, “…you may slaughter and eat meat within any of your gates…” (Deuteronomy 12:15). Any of their gates works. The word only isn't there.
Moses doesn't say outside the camp. He says, “…you may slaughter and eat meat within any of your gates…” (Deuteronomy 12:15). Within means inside, friend. Their own gates are the place.

Moses says, “Both the ceremonially clean and unclean may eat it as they would a gazelle or deer…” (Deuteronomy 12:15). Clean and unclean are both welcome at this table. No one gets turned away at the door.

The text says it's true. Moses says, “Both the ceremonially clean and unclean may eat it as they would a gazelle or deer…” (Deuteronomy 12:15). Both are welcome to eat that meat. Nobody is left out of this one.
Moses says, “…but you must not eat the blood; pour it on the ground like water.” (Deuteronomy 12:16). That's the one firm limit. Everything else is open, but not the blood.
Moses doesn't mention skin. He says, “…but you must not eat the blood; pour it on the ground like water.” (Deuteronomy 12:16). The limit is the blood. The skin isn't part of this verse.
Bones aren't named here. Moses says, “…but you must not eat the blood; pour it on the ground like water.” (Deuteronomy 12:16). The blood is the one thing off the menu. No bones about it, friend.

Moses says the opposite: “Within your gates you must not eat the tithe of your grain or new wine or oil, the firstborn of your herds or flocks, any of the offerings that you have vowed to give, or your freewill offerings or special gifts.” (Deuteronomy 12:17). Those are not everyday meat. They have a different place to be eaten, and that place isn't home.

That's right. Moses says, “Within your gates you must not eat the tithe of your grain or new wine or oil, the firstborn of your herds or flocks, any of the offerings that you have vowed to give, or your freewill offerings or special gifts.” (Deuteronomy 12:17). Everyday meat and these gifts are not the same, and the text keeps them apart. Home is for one, not the other.

explanations.answer: In the LORD's presence at His chosen place
explanations.explanation: Moses says, “Instead, you must eat them in the presence of the LORD your God at the place the LORD your God will choose…” (Deuteronomy 12:18). The Levite is named among those eating there too. Same chosen place, same presence.

explanations.answer: In the home of the nearest Levite
explanations.explanation: Moses doesn't send them to a Levite's house. He says to eat them “in the presence of the LORD your God at the place the LORD your God will choose…” (Deuteronomy 12:18). The Levite is named as one of those eating there with them. The place is the LORD's chosen place.

explanations.answer: At the edge of their own fields
explanations.explanation: No field edges in this verse. Moses says, “you must eat them in the presence of the LORD your God at the place the LORD your God will choose…” (Deuteronomy 12:18). That's the place. Their fields aren't it.

Moses says, “…be careful not to neglect the Levites as long as you live in your land.” (Deuteronomy 12:19). The Levites show up twice, once at the table and once in a warning. That tells me Moses wants them remembered.

Follow doesn't fit the verse. Moses says, “…be careful not to neglect the Levites as long as you live in your land.” (Deuteronomy 12:19). The word is neglect. Nobody is told to follow the Levites in this verse.
Question isn't the word Moses uses. He says, “…be careful not to neglect the Levites as long as you live in your land.” (Deuteronomy 12:19). The word is neglect. No quizzing involved, friend.

Moses says the opposite. If the place is too far, “then you may slaughter any of the herd or flock He has given you… and you may eat it within your gates whenever you want.” (Deuteronomy 12:21). No waiting for a trip. Home works just fine.

Right, Moses doesn't make them wait. He says, “If the place where the LORD your God chooses to put His Name is too far from you, then you may slaughter any of the herd or flock He has given you, as I have commanded you, and you may eat it within your gates whenever you want.” (Deuteronomy 12:21). So distance doesn't hold up the meal.

Moses says, “Only be sure not to eat the blood, because the blood is the life, and you must not eat the life with the meat.” (Deuteronomy 12:23). That's his reason, friend. The meat is fine, but the life isn't on the menu.

explanations.answer: The blood belongs to the priests
explanations.explanation: Moses doesn't say that. His reason is, “…because the blood is the life, and you must not eat the life with the meat.” (Deuteronomy 12:23). The blood is tied to life. Priests aren't mentioned in the verse.

explanations.answer: The blood makes the meat unclean
explanations.explanation: That's not the reason given. Moses says, “…because the blood is the life, and you must not eat the life with the meat.” (Deuteronomy 12:23). Earlier, he even says clean and unclean may eat the meat (Deuteronomy 12:22). The reason is that the blood is the life.

explanations.answer: Them and their children after them
explanations.explanation: Moses says, “Do not eat it, so that it may go well with you and your children after you…” (Deuteronomy 12:25). It's about them and their children after them. I think that's a nice thing to hear from a preacher.

explanations.answer: Them and the Levites among them
explanations.explanation: The Levites are in other verses, but not this one. Moses says, “Do not eat it, so that it may go well with you and your children after you…” (Deuteronomy 12:25). The ones named are Israel and their children after them.

explanations.answer: Them and the foreigners among them
explanations.explanation: Foreigners aren't named in that verse. Moses says, “Do not eat it, so that it may go well with you and your children after you…” (Deuteronomy 12:25). So it's Israel and their children after them. Nobody else is on that line.

Moses says, “The blood of your other sacrifices must be poured out beside the altar of the LORD your God, but you may eat the meat.” (Deuteronomy 12:27). The burnt offering gets both meat and blood on the altar. For the other sacrifices, the people eat the meat. Good news for the table.

explanations.answer: It is burned on the altar
explanations.explanation: That belongs to the burnt offerings. Moses says to present “the meat and blood of your burnt offerings on the altar” (Deuteronomy 12:27). But for the other sacrifices, “…you may eat the meat.” So that meat isn't burned.

This verse doesn't say that. Moses says, “The blood of your other sacrifices must be poured out beside the altar of the LORD your God, but you may eat the meat.” (Deuteronomy 12:27). The meat is for eating, and the verse names no one else. Don't add a name to it, friend.

explanations.answer: Asking how they served their gods
explanations.explanation: Moses says, “Do not inquire about their gods, asking, ‘How do these nations serve their gods? I will do likewise.’” (Deuteronomy 12:30). The trap is the asking, then copying. He doesn't want Israel curious about it in that way.

explanations.answer: Asking how they farmed their land
explanations.explanation: Farming isn't the trap in this verse. Moses warns about asking, “How do these nations serve their gods? I will do likewise.” (Deuteronomy 12:30). The trap is about their gods. The land isn't the issue.

explanations.answer: Copying how they built their cities
explanations.explanation: City building isn't what Moses brings up. He warns against asking, “How do these nations serve their gods? I will do likewise.” (Deuteronomy 12:30). The warning is about worship. Cities don't come into it.

explanations.answer: Not to add to them or subtract from them
explanations.explanation: Moses says, “See that you do everything I command you; do not add to it or subtract from it.” (Deuteronomy 12:32). Nothing added, nothing taken away. That's a clean recipe, friend.

explanations.answer: To change them when the times change
explanations.explanation: Moses says nothing about changing them. He says, “See that you do everything I command you; do not add to it or subtract from it.” (Deuteronomy 12:32). The commands stay as given. No edits on the fly.

explanations.answer: To keep the parts that fit them best
explanations.explanation: No picking and choosing in that verse. Moses says, “See that you do everything I command you; do not add to it or subtract from it.” (Deuteronomy 12:32). Everything means everything. You don't get to skip the part that's hard to stamp.
